title: Untrimmed output reference and box-method temperature coefficient over -40..125 degC
claim: README.md 'Target specification (DRAFT)' rows 'Output reference' (1.20 V +/-1% untrimmed) and 'Temp coefficient (-40...125 degC)' (< 50 ppm/degC), for the 3.3 V primary flavor (DR-001). Records are PROVISIONAL against the draft spec until issue #1 ratifies it. Measures design/bandgap_core.sch open-circuit, untrimmed (no trim network -- that is issue #13), across process and supply corners with temperature swept continuously inside the deck.
statistical_convention: N/A (corner-matrix claim, not a distribution claim -- untrimmed spread from local mismatch is issue #12's Monte Carlo)

analyses: meas dc vref27 FIND v(vref) AT=27

measurements.name: vref_27
measurements.note: Untrimmed open-circuit reference at 27 degC, read off the in-deck temperature sweep. Window is the draft spec's 1.20 V +/-1%. 27 degC is not on the 11 degC sweep grid (-40, -29, -18, ... 114, 125), so this is ngspice's linear interpolation between the 26 degC and 37 degC points; on a curve whose total excursion is tens of mV over 165 degC the interpolation error is of order 50 uV (~0.004% of 1.2 V), more than two orders of magnitude inside the +/-1% window.

measurements.name: vref_min
measurements.note: Minimum of VREF over the -40..125 degC sweep. Bounds are a loose +/-5% sanity band, not the spec window: the spec line is on the 27 degC value and on the TC derived from this excursion. A value outside +/-5% means the curve left the bandgap regime somewhere in the range and the TC number below would be meaningless.

measurements.name: vref_max
measurements.note: Maximum of VREF over the -40..125 degC sweep; same loose sanity band as vref_min.

measurements.name: tc_ppm
measurements.note: Box-method TC: peak-to-peak VREF excursion over -40..125 degC, normalized to VREF(27 degC) and to the 165 degC span. Limit is the draft spec's < 50 ppm/degC target column; the < 20 ppm/degC stretch column is out of scope for wave 1 per DR-001's scope note.

measurements.name: n_temp_points
measurements.note: Guard: asserts the in-deck temperature sweep really produced 16 points (-40..125 degC at 11 degC). If the sweep silently collapsed to a single operating point, the box TC above would read 0 ppm/degC and look like a spectacular pass. This check makes that failure loud.

spread_checks.note: VREF(27 degC) must move by at least 0.1 mV across the process/supply matrix. A dead-flat result across 15 corner points means the corner include or the supply param is not reaching the simulator.

notes: Temperature is swept INSIDE the deck (dc temp -40 125 11) because the box method needs the peak-to-peak excursion of a continuous curve; a three-point outer axis would miss the curvature extremum, which for a bandgap generally sits between the endpoints. The runner is therefore invoked with --temp 27 --subset-reason; process and supply run in full (5 x 3 = 15 points).

Grid resolution is 11 degC (16 points), chosen so the sweep lands exactly on both endpoints (-40 + 15*11 = 125) -- the endpoints are where a bandgap characteristic is furthest from its extremum, so a grid that misses 125 degC would systematically under-report the box excursion. Rationale for the coarseness: the VREF(T) characteristic is smooth and near-quadratic, so an 11 degC grid can miss the interior extremum by at most 5.5 degC; with this core's measured curvature (~30 mV of excursion over 165 degC, i.e. a quadratic coefficient of order 4e-6 V/degC^2) that costs at most ~0.13 mV of peak-to-peak, i.e. under 1 ppm/degC on a TC of order 100 ppm/degC. Every ngspice temperature step forces a full re-evaluation of the PDK model set's temperature-dependent parameters, which dominates runtime; finer grids buy nothing measurable. Cross-check on the coarseness: a bring-up run of the same deck at 33 degC resolution (6 points) at tt / 27 degC / 3.30 V reported 164.5 ppm/degC, so the number is not an artifact of the grid.
The corner axes above declare the full PVT matrix so the manifest stays the canonical statement of what the claim requires and the subset is visible as a subset in the record.

Solver tolerances are tightened well past ngspice's defaults: reltol=1e-6 (default 1e-3), vntol=1e-9 (default 1e-6), abstol=1e-15 (default 1e-12). This is a MEASUREMENT-RESOLUTION requirement, not a taste preference. At the default reltol=1e-3 the DC solver is only obliged to converge a ~1.175 V node to ~1.2 mV, and the first run of sim/line-regulation/ (record 20260803-100723-77b96e3) duly reported a 0.11 .. 1.27 mV supply-induced output shift that, on inspection of the raw sweep, was non-monotonic point-to-point jitter at exactly that amplitude -- i.e. the solver's convergence noise floor, not a property of the circuit. Re-run with these tolerances the same sweep is smooth and monotone with a shallow minimum near 3.45 V, and the shift drops to tens of microvolts. Every DC-based bench in this suite shares the setting so that all four are read off the same, resolved operating point.
